newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AMP's Ergo to use NZ Post outlets.
newsitem.headline: AMP's Ergo to use NZ Post outlets.

text.p: AMP Society's Ergo subsidiary said on Tuesday it had signed an agency agreement with state-owned New Zealand Post allowing customers to open Ergo term deposit and call accounts at 297 Post shops nationwide.
The service will be available from Monday.

Ergo was set up in 1995 as a telephone bank, but managing director Graham Meyer said the company recognised some people preferred to deposit their funds in person, rather than transfer funds electronically or send cheques through the mail.
"Ergo wanted the benefit of a branch network but not the cost of establishing one," Meyer said.
With 297 shops, NZ Post provided one of New Zealand's largest branch networks.
Meyer said Ergo's move contrasted with other banks, which were closing branches in provincial towns and suburbs.
The company would continue to assess whether other retail outlets could be added to Ergo's network. It also planned to improve its Internet capability in the next few months.
Ergo said it expected to increase its customer base and market share significantly via the NZ Post network.
New Zealand Post group manager consumer Patrick Denham said the deal was the first stage of a move into agency banking for his company.
NZ Post already provided an agency for paying a number of household bills, including car re-licensing and road user charges, he said.
The deal with Ergo would give New Zealand Post the chance to gauge demand from customers and other financial institutions for this type of agency service.
